body: claimed: Codex (skull) · 2026-11-20T15:33Z · branch mkinney:issue/2996-wide-verdict · plan: widen each gouge law's tolerance by how far a reduced model's chord passes DEV_TOL, up to a 0.02 mm chord; collision bands still grow by the full excess; name the tolerance in a program header comment and in the model note. The law reads any recorded chord, so the code does not wait for #2994.

Fact from the review of PR #2994: the document does not record why a model has reduced accuracy. The component `ReducedFidelity` holds only `chord_mm`. Two causes give a coarse model: the STEP facet budget (#1054) and edges that lie off their surfaces (#2976). Thus PR #2994 makes each advice text name the two remedies: "re-import with a larger STEP facet budget, or export the file again with a tighter tolerance". This issue adds a per-model fidelity record. Add the cause to that record (and the measured deviation). Then each text names the one cause.

Design note (read-only Opus review, not built).

Read on `origin/issue/2976-edge-gap-cap` (head 364e4b4f4). Nothing was built or run.

## Design summary

- Scope: a model that the importer meshed coarse because of the file's own stated tolerance (the #2976 path). Call it a "reduced-accuracy model". A model that the facet budget made coarse keeps the #864 law.
- Rule: on a reduced-accuracy model with a chord at or under `ACCURACY_LIMIT_MM` = 0.02 mm, every gouge law reads the normal tolerance against the mesh. The law does not subtract the excess and does not add it. The post is permitted, and the program header says that the model is at reduced accuracy.
- Cost, stated in the note: a check against the mesh can miss a cut into the true surface of up to `DEV_TOL` + chord = 0.030 mm. Today the bound is `DEV_TOL` + `CHORD_CAP` = 0.015 mm.
- A fact found here: today NO operation posts on such a model, roughing included. `floor_of` does not read the stock to leave (`fidelity_law.rs:181-186`), so `op_problem` refuses each excess-aware operation (`model_fidelity.rs:338-340`). Also, `verdict_tol` refuses the program (`model_fidelity.rs:359-363`). The issue body says that roughing with stock to leave is a workaround. The code does not agree.

## Verdict tolerance

- Value: the chord (`ReducedFidelity.chord_mm`), not the measured deviation. The kernel certifies deviation + `SNAP_MOVE_MM` <= chord (`crates/kernel/src/machining_mesh.rs:320-322`). The measured bound is one-sided (`docs/decisions/917-kernel-parity.md:98-103`). The chord costs 0.0005 mm on `Lobe.step` (0.020 against 0.0195) and needs no new number.
- Storage: a new optional field `ReducedFidelity.file_tol_mm: Option<f64>` (`crates/app/src/schema.rs:102-104`). It holds the tolerance that the file states, and it is `Some` only when the importer meshed looser for it.
  - Source: `loosened` in `crates/geometry/src/step.rs:104-151`. Add `StepMesh.file_tol_mm`, then `Graded.file_tol_mm` (`crates/app/src/geometry/import/mod.rs:90-110`), then `model_fidelity::set`.
  - Project file: an optional field with serde default `None`, beside `coarse_mm` (`crates/app/src/project/wire.rs:179-181`).
  - Fail-safe: a path that drops the field (a copy, a clone, undo, an old file) falls back to the #864 law. That law is stricter, so a lost field never loosens a check.
- `ACCURACY_LIMIT_MM` = 0.02 is a `const` in `model_fidelity.rs`. No file value raises it. Add a const assert that it equals `EDGE_GAP_LIMIT_MM`.
- What `verdict_tol` (`model_fidelity.rs:396-410`) returns. It reads each model and takes the smallest result; the first `Err` wins.

| Model | `verdict_tol` | Excess given to the generation laws |
|---|---|---|
| Full fidelity | `Ok(DEV_TOL)`, unchanged | 0, unchanged |
| Budget-coarsened (`file_tol_mm` is `None`) | #864, unchanged: `DEV_TOL - excess`, or `Err` | `chord - CHORD_CAP`, unchanged |
| Reduced accuracy, chord <= 0.02 (`Lobe.step`: 0.020) | `Ok(DEV_TOL)` | 0 |
| Reduced accuracy, chord > 0.02 (a facet budget made it coarser) | `Err`, refusal by name | not used: `op_problem` refuses |
| Unknown fidelity | `Err`, unchanged | not used |

- `op_problem` (`model_fidelity.rs:327-341`): for a reduced-accuracy model it keeps the `excess_aware` refusal (`:333-336`). Swarf, the cone and engrave rides, wire and sinker stay refused. The `excess_floor` test reads excess 0.
- Why budget-coarsened models keep #864: they have a cure (a larger facet budget), and the advice text says so. A reduced-accuracy model has no cure in CamCraft. Only a new export of the file can cure it.

## Direction rule

Sign: `v = sim - mesh` (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/deviate.rs:78-90`). Rest when `v > tol`, gouge when `v < -tol`. Only a gouge blocks the post (`crates/app/src/posting_sim.rs:86`). Rest never blocks.

(a) Gouge side. Let `c` be the chord. On a convex wall the chord mesh stands inside the true surface by up to `c` (`model_fidelity.rs:5-8`). A real gouge `g` reads `v = -(g - c)` there. Thus a gouge passes up to `T + c`.
- Measured case (chord 0.02, deviation 0.0195):
  - Recommended (`T` = `DEV_TOL` against the mesh): up to 0.030 mm by the chord (0.0295 by the deviation) can pass.
  - Symmetric widening to `T` = d: up to 2 x 0.0195 = 0.039 mm. Rejected: it counts the deviation in favour of the tool two times.
  - A strict bound of 0.02 mm on the real gouge: `T` = 0.02 - 0.0195 = 0.0005 mm (0 by the chord). That is less than the path tolerance of any finishing pass, so a finishing pass at zero stock is refused again. With a new law that reads the stock to leave, the smallest stock to leave that posts is `DEV_TOL` + c - 0.02 = 0.010 mm. To keep the 0.015 mm line of today, it is 0.015 mm. No such law exists today.
- Recommended: `T` = `DEV_TOL`. The check adds nothing in favour of the tool. The only extra is the offset `c` of the mesh itself, which no check against the mesh can see. The program note states it.
- Result: a finishing pass at zero stock posts. The generator and every check read the same mesh, so a pass that touches the mesh reads `v` near 0. On a concave wall the mesh stands outside the material, so a pass on the mesh leaves up to `c` of material. That is rest, not a false refusal.
- A real gouge of the mesh deeper than `DEV_TOL` still blocks. A gouge of the true surface deeper than 0.030 mm always blocks.

(b) Rest side: keep `DEV_TOL`. A wider rest tolerance is safe, but rest does not block the post, so it gains nothing. The colour map does not change. `deviate` keeps one `tol`.

(c) The other readers. Each reads the effective excess, which is 0 for a reduced-accuracy model:
- `section.rs` law (b) (`cx.tightened(cx.gouge_tol)` reads plain), the solid law (`generate.rs:3955`), the mark law (`mark_law.rs:200`), the envelope law (f), the meridian scans, `stock_top.rs`: they judge as on a full model.
- The program sim and the stock view (`stock_sim.rs:71`, `stock_sim_carry.rs:332`, `stock_play.rs:113,225`, `stock_view.rs:248-253`) get `Ok(DEV_TOL)` through `program_tol`.
- Clearance laws (holder, shank, rapids, bar feed, stylus, the cross-drill bands through `band_growth`, the collision checks against the stock): give them the RAW excess as band growth, with no tolerance floor. A larger band never convicts a finished face, so it is free. The worker lists each clearance reader that takes `model_excess` and confirms it grows a band and does not shrink a cutting tolerance.
- Put this in one place: `fidelity_law::contact_excess(world, model)` and `clearance_excess(...)`, read by `material.rs:129,240`. Do not add a second derivation in the laws.

## Program note

- Carrier: a new field `notes: Vec<String>` in `camcraft_post::post::js_host::ProgramId` (`crates/post/src/post/js_host.rs:170-180`). `set_program` (`js.rs:198-202`) writes it as `program.notes`. The app fills it in `posting_program.rs:109` from `model_fidelity::program_notes(world)`.
- Each shipped post prints `program.notes` in `onOpen`, in its own comment form, beside `invertedNotes()` (the precedent, `fanuc.cps:552-559,577`).
- Law in the engine: after `onOpen` (`engine.rs:151-152`), each note must be in the header text. If a note is not there, the post is refused: `post script '<name>' does not print the model note; this program cannot post without it`. Thus a user script cannot drop the note silently.
- Text: printable ASCII, no `( ) % ;`, each line at or under 40 characters (`clean` cuts at 40, `fanuc.cps:516-519`). Numbers are in the program unit.
  - `REDUCED ACCURACY MODEL <name, cleaned, max 17>`
  - `MESH WITHIN 0.020 MM OF SURFACES`
  - `CHECKED TO 0.030 MM OF SURFACES`
- UI line (model page, `summary`, `model_fidelity.rs:272-277`): "Reduced accuracy: the surfaces of this model are approximated to within 0.020 mm, the tolerance that its file states. Checks against it can miss a cut of up to 0.030 mm into the true surface. Programs on it say so in their header. To clear this, export the file again with a tighter tolerance."
- The post result and the status line show the same sentence as a note that does not block.
- Correct the advice text for this class: no "larger STEP facet budget" (`model_fidelity.rs:58,294,335`, review blocker 2 on PR #2994).

## Pins

- `reduced_accuracy_model_posts_a_finish_with_the_note` (`crates/app/tests/model_accuracy_post.rs`): `edge_gap_018_stated_010.step` (chord 0.020), Finish3D at zero stock. The post is `Ok`. The header has the three lines exactly. `verdict_tol` is `Ok(DEV_TOL)`.
- `reduced_accuracy_model_over_the_limit_is_refused_by_name`: the same fixture with a facet budget that makes the chord larger than 0.02 mm, or a set component with chord 0.0201 and `file_tol_mm`. `gate_problems` names the model and "over the 0.020 mm limit".
- `a_real_gouge_on_a_reduced_accuracy_model_still_blocks`: a cut 0.02 mm under the model floor on the fixture. The post is refused with the `gouge: program cuts below the model` line.
- `budget_coarsened_model_keeps_the_864_law`: chord 0.012 without `file_tol_mm` gives `DEV_TOL - 0.007`.
- `a_project_without_file_tol_reads_the_864_law`: an old file loads with `None`, so the law is stricter.
- `reduced_accuracy_texts`: `summary`, `facts`, the refusal text, no facet-budget advice. Also update the UI label test `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/model_fidelity.rs:11-24`.
- `crates/post/tests`: `a_script_that_drops_the_program_notes_is_refused`, and `every_shipped_post_prints_the_program_notes` (one recorded `.cnc` for each kind that the script serves).
- Unchanged and green: `crates/app/tests/model_fidelity.rs:206-231`, `fidelity_copies.rs:210-247`, `step_fidelity.rs`, `import_step_open_shell.rs:162`.

## Work split

- PR 1, `camcraft-post` only: `ProgramId.notes`, `set_program`, the engine header law, and each `assets/posts/*.cps`. It does not need #2994 and can start now. `effort:high` (it changes posted G-code).
- PR 2, `camcraft-geometry` + `camcraft-app` (+ a UI text test): `file_tol_mm` from the importer to the component and the project file, the law in `model_fidelity.rs` and `fidelity_law.rs`, the texts, the notes, and the pins. `camcraft-sim` does not change (`deviate`, `excess_floor` stay). It needs PR #2994 on `main`, then PR 1. `effort:max` (safety floor).
- The decision file `docs/decisions/2996-reduced-accuracy-verdict.md` names the rule, the 0.02 mm limit, and the 0.030 mm bound that the user loses.

## Questions for the maintainer

1. Do you accept a real-surface bound of 0.030 mm (`DEV_TOL` + chord) on a reduced-accuracy model, stated in the header, so that a finishing pass at zero stock posts? Recommended: yes. A strict 0.02 mm bound refuses finishing again (0.0005 mm margin).
2. Does the new law apply only to models meshed coarse by the file's own tolerance, while facet-budget models keep #864? Recommended: yes, because those models have a cure in CamCraft.
3. Is a post script that does not print the model note refused for such a program? Recommended: yes. Otherwise a custom post drops the note silently.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

The maintainer answered the three questions of the design note (2026-11-20). The decision file of each PR for this issue records them.

1. Yes. On a model of this kind, a cut of up to 0.030 mm into the true surface can pass. The program header states this. A finishing pass at zero stock then posts.
2. Yes. The new law applies only to a model that the importer meshed more coarsely because of the tolerance that the file states. A model that the facet budget made coarse keeps the law of #864.
3. No. This is not the recommended answer of the design note. A custom post that does not print the model note is NOT refused. The posts that ship with the application print the note. Consequence: a program from a custom post can be without the warning. The decision file states this consequence, and the documentation for post authors says how to print the note.

One correction to the issue body: today no operation posts on such a model, roughing included. The roughing check does not read the stock to leave.

Work order: PR 1 changes `camcraft-post` only (the `notes` field of the program record, and the shipped posts print it). PR 2 has the law and the texts, and it needs PR #2994 on `main`.
